subject: POC plan + blocking issues and mitigation playbook (Acme Analytics)
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana@acme.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial POC discussion follow-up

Markus / team,

Thanks for the call this morning — appreciate the clear framing. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can mobilize our data science team: 

Summary of what we want to evaluate in the 3-week POC:
- Inference latency at 95th percentile under our batch mixes (short queries ~30 tokens, long queries ~600 tokens)
- Cost per 1k tokens under expected throughput patterns (burst + steady state)
- Quality on our analytics prompts (we'll share 40 reference prompts)
- Integration validity: ability to run on our VPC and access S3-like datastore

Risk concerns we flagged on the call:
1) Any runtime optimizations that rely on KV-cache persistence — we need determinism for token billing and reproducibility in evals.
2) Network egress / peering: can you confirm region-to-region routing?
3) Data deletion guarantees for temp caches (audit requirement)

Requests / next steps:
- Please send a concrete POC success criteria matrix and an evaluation plan with ownerships and timelines (we'd like to start next Monday).
- Add a row for what happens if a blocking bug appears (escalation path).

Attachments: I attached the POC intake template we use.

Thanks,
Dana Liu
Head of Applied ML
Acme Analytics
[Attachment: acme-poc-intake-template.xlsx (xlsx, 28 KB)]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <dana@acme.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos@acme.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial POC discussion follow-up

Dana — thanks for the clear recap. We can definitely run the POC starting next Monday (2026-06-28). Below is our proposed POC plan + success matrix and a mitigation playbook for blocking issues. I've kept timelines tight but feasible. Please confirm owners on your side for the prompt set + infra access.

POC high-level timeline:
- Week 0 (prep, by 2026-06-27): access + baseline tests, share prompt set, confirm S3/VPC peering window
- Week 1 (pilot): baseline latency/cost measurements on sample traffic
- Week 2 (scale): higher throughput profile + stability tests, run full quality evals
- Week 3 (wrap): final evaluation, recommendations, and rollout checklist

Success criteria (pass/fail per row):
- Latency: P95 < 450ms for short queries; P95 < 1.2s for long queries (with specified batch settings)
- Cost: unit token cost reduction target vs your current baseline (we'll quantify after baseline run)
- Quality: >= 85% agreement with your reference answers on core prompts (we'll agree on metric: exact match / F1)
- Security: VPC peering established and audit logs available for temp storage

Blocking-issue mitigation playbook (short form):
- Symptom: KV-cache corruption or incorrect token outputs observed during pilot.
  - Immediate mitigation: disable persistent KV cache for affected routes; switch to single-request execution (owner: Grace O'Connor, 2 hrs)
  - Workaround: force-run on fallback model variant without cache optimizations (owner: Markus Klein, 4 hrs)
  - Escalation: open high-priority ticket with Runtime SRE and engage model-infra patch (target SLA: 24 hrs for bugfix, notify customer hourly)
- Symptom: Network peering failure affecting >30% of requests.
  - Immediate mitigation: route to hosted-region fallback in same geography (owner: Monica Patel, 1 hr)
  - Escalation: Cloud network team + customer infra lead for permanent route (target: 48 hrs)

Attachments: POC matrix (starter) + network diagram stub attached. I'll upload a refined version after I hear back on owners.

Proposed immediate asks for Acme:
1) Confirm prompt owners (name + email) for the 40-reference prompts.
2) Provide a 2-hour peering window for baseline tests next Monday morning PT.
3) Confirm any compliance checkpoints we should pre-provide (SOC2 artifact pointers).

I'll follow up with a short recorded walkthrough of the evaluation dashboard.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme-poc-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Liu <dana@acme.ai>, Carlos Mendez <carlos@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial POC discussion follow-up

Markus / team — quick technical notes to ensure the mitigation playbook is actionable: 

1) Disabling KV cache (short-term mitigation) will increase latency on long-run streaming calls; we should quantify the delta in the pilot and include a fall-back configuration so Acme can see the trade-offs. I'll prepare a config matrix.
2) For the fallback model variant, suggest we pre-share an image of the model (quantized 8-bit) and a pinned runner so switching is a single flag flip. That reduces the 4-hr manual window to ~30 minutes for warmup.
3) Logging: we'll enable request-level debug logging for 48 hrs on the pilot project ID. We need Acme's confirmation on retention TTL (we can mask inputs).

I'll own the runtime toggles and the short playbook runbook. Markus — can you take point on commercial notice (what we do if we miss the P95 target) so we have a unified message?

-G

Grace O'Connor
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Mendez <carlos@acme.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Liu <dana@acme.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial POC discussion follow-up

Thanks Markus / Grace — this looks good and thorough. A few clarifications from our infra team: 

- Prompt owners: myself and Dana will own the prompt set (Carlos.d@acme.ai, Dana.l@acme.ai). We'll deliver the 40 prompts by Friday (2026-06-25).
- Peering window confirmed: Monday 2026-06-28, 08:00-10:00 PT.
- Audit logs: we require a 30-day retention for temporary debug logs, masked at token level (if possible).

On the blocking-bug playbook: what does "open high-priority ticket" mean in practice? Can we get an escalation contact and SLAs for notification cadence? We need to include that in our internal risk register.

Also — if the persistent KV cache causes nondeterministic outputs (we flagged this as a compliance risk) will Redwood provide a signed statement of mitigation steps and timeline if we detect reproducibility failures?

Happy to jump on a 30-minute runbook alignment call if helpful.

-Carlos

--
Carlos Mendez
Lead ML Engineer, Acme Analytics

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos@acme.ai>, Dana Liu <dana@acme.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial POC discussion follow-up

Carlos / Dana — thanks, good to have prompt owners and the peering window. Quick answers and next steps: 

Escalation and notification cadence: 
- Primary escalation contact (Redwood Runtime SRE): SRE Pager — sreruntime@redwood.ai (monitored 24/7).
- On detection of a blocking bug (defined as >20% request failure rate or incorrect outputs on reference prompts):
  - Immediate acknowledgement: within 15 minutes (channel: shared Slack #acme-poc and email to customer ops)
  - Hourly status updates until mitigation applied
  - Targeted bugfix timeline: 24 hours for hotfix; follow-up permanent patch within 7 days depending on root cause
- We'll provide a written mitigation statement if nondeterminism is observed. That will include root cause, steps taken, and a remediation ETA signed by our Head of Runtime Engineering.

Commercial fallback if we miss agreed P95 targets: we will offer a 2-week extension of the trial and provide cost credits proportional to the time impacted (details in trial SOW). I'll draft the short commercial notice language and share by EOD.

Action items (owner / due):
- Acme: deliver 40 prompts + test data access (Carlos / Dana) — due 2026-06-25 EOD
- Redwood: finalize POC matrix + runbook with explicit toggle commands (Grace) — due 2026-06-25 noon PT
- Redwood: draft short mitigation statement template and commercial fallback wording (Markus) — due 2026-06-24 EOD (attached draft)
- Both: short kickoff call to confirm peering window and runbook (30 minutes) — propose 2026-06-26 10:00 PT

If that all looks good I'll lock calendar invites and share the Drive folder with artifacts.

Thanks — looking forward to starting.

-Markus

Markus Klein
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
[Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB_example_drive_link]
Note: All messages above include typical Gmail quoting and signatures. Attachments referenced as stubs.
thread_summary: Sales thread coordinating a 3-week POC with Acme Analytics. Plan includes explicit success criteria (latency, cost, quality, security), a mitigation playbook for blocking issues (KV-cache corruption, peering failures), owners (Grace for runtime toggles, Markus for commercial notices, Monica for networking), timeline (start 2026-06-28), and escalation cadence (SRE Pager + hourly updates).
